correctness.rationale: Exact quadratic-integer line-coordinate arithmetic recovers all 210 pairs as 21 quadruple plus 28 triple points, 70 rational components, 168 nodes, and genus 99. Weighted 20x20 Bareiss determinant and spectral identity independently fix spanning-tree factorization 2^26*3^23*7^5*719^6. Full p-local Smith reductions modulo sufficient p-powers, using two independently chosen deleted vertices, agree and give unit factors 60 with remaining 4,72,216,155304,1087128 repeated five times. A standard Raynaud theorem applies only to the claimed thickness-one regular semistable smoothing class; a standalone exact verifier and actual output are packaged.

originality.rationale: Full 70-vertex incidence boundary rather than either 42-vertex quadruple-only or 49-vertex triple-only Klein configuration. Material inspection of Seceleanu (2014, Section 4.2), Gévay–Pokora (2022/2023, geometric incidence/rigidity and derived configurations), and Innamorati (2024, Section 4) supports that these sources do not state the complete integral Laplacian invariant factors. Existing related calculations of the partial configuration critical groups concern different Laplacians and do not logically imply this 719-primary group. General Raynaud component-group theorem does not evaluate the matrix. This is a best-knowledge priority judgment, subject to hidden-table risk. The same-blowup primary study arXiv:1609.08648 was additionally inspected in full text; its negative curves/point-ideal results do not calculate the complete dual-graph Smith decomposition.
residual_risks: A specialist historical table or graph-alias publication may already record the full 70-vertex Smith form, despite broad current searches.
The generic Raynaud identification requires a proper regular semistable model and unit thickness; results for other models differ.
Full PDF of an additional 2022 manuscript was not accessible at the arXiv PDF endpoint, although its available extensive full-text transcription was inspected.

value.rationale: Blowing up all 49 multiple points is a canonical stable normal-crossings boundary of the classical Klein reflection arrangement; its 99-dimensional graph cycle space is a natural Jacobian degeneration object. The full integral Néron group is a meaningful exact arithmetic invariant not determined by numerical incidence/spectrum or the two known partial-configuration groups, and reveals six copies of 719-primary torsion. Its precise decomposition may inform comparisons among stable degenerations and graph-Jacobian specializations without requiring a downstream theorem.
